content.title: Shorthanded Lakers knock off Durant-less Rockets in Game 1 - Los Angeles Times
content.text: Even if they were missing their starting backcourt of Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, the Lakers were committed to being resilient and poised against the rugged and physical Houston Rockets in Game 1 of their playoff series.As a group the Lakers were, and they followed the lead of LeBron James and a career-best outing from Luke Kennard to pull out a gritty 107-98 win Saturday night at Crypto.com Arena.“Just thought we were really poised as a team,” coach JJ Redick said. “We had a great next-play mentality. Wasn’t a perfect game. None of these games are gonna be perfect. Got contributions from a lot of people in a lot of different ways and made enough winning plays, despite the turnovers and the offensive rebounds.”James was magnificent as the leader of the Lakers, collecting a near triple-double with 19 points on nine-for-15 shooting, 13 assists and eight rebounds.Kennard was outstanding in his new role as facilitator and a main hub of the offense, scoring a playoff career-high 27 points. His three three-pointers in the fourth quarter gave the Lakers the separation they needed to lead the best-of-seven series that resumes here Tuesday night. He was five for five from three-point range — after leading the league for the third time — and nine for 13 overall.James tied Hall of Famers Karl Malone and John Stockton for the record by beginning his 19th postseason, and he and Kennard had plenty of help from the Lakers’ other starters.Deandre Ayton had a double-double with 19 points and 11 rebounds, Marcus Smart had 15 points and eight assists, and Rui Hachimura scored 14.“We don’t have a choice. It has to be that way. It has to be a collective group,” said James, who had eight assists in the first quarter, his career high for any quarter of a playoff game. “When you’re missing so much firepower, like we are right now with AR and Luka being out, we all have to pitch in. We all have to do our job. And even do a little bit more. Protect one another offensively and defensively, and I think we did that tonight.”The Lakers started the game with purpose, making 15 of 19 shots in the first quarter — 78.9%. Kennard was the best, making five of six for 11 points to help the Lakers open a 33-29 lead. But the game slowed down in the second quarter when the Lakers scored just 17 points to the Rockets’ 19. Injured Rockets star Kevin Durant, third from left on bench, watches Lakers star LeBron James inbound the basketball during Game 1. (Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times) The Rockets took the lead to open the second half, but the Lakers used a balanced attack to take a 75-66 lead into the fourth quarter and quickly pulled away.The Rockets, playing without Kevin Durant, shot 38% and were held to their fewest points since a 100-92 loss to the Lakers on March 16.Forty minutes before tipoff, Doncic walked down the hallway with his bodyguard toward the locker room. Doncic was returning to the team after getting treatment for his hamstring strain in Europe, but not playing, joining Reaves (oblique strain) on the bench in street clothes.They were not the only stars sitting out as Durant, the Rockets’ All-Star forward and leading scorer at 26 points per game, missed the game because of a right knee contusion. Durant worked out before the game but was unable to play because of “soreness and tenderness,” coach Ime Udoka said. The Rockets hope he’ll be available for Game 2.“Bumped a knee in practice one of our days, on Wednesday,” Udoka said. “Hopefully it’s a one-game thing, but [he] tried it out just shortly ago and didn’t feel good enough.”For the Lakers, there was an element of shock they had to overcome when Doncic and Reaves were injured at Oklahoma City on April 2. The Lakers eventually got past that, winning their last three games of the regular season.They had a game plan for Durant for the playoffs, but the Lakers quickly made another shift once they learned he was out, even overcoming 20 turnovers and the 21 offensive rebounds the Rockets collected.“Again, this is all we’ve talked about for two months, is just our playoff mentality,” Redick said. “You can’t worry about who’s in or out of the lineup. It’s our game plan, it’s our standards, it’s how we play. And we’ve built toward that. And I thought our guys just responded well and met the moment. I mean, that’s the biggest thing: You got to meet the moment in every game. And they were able to do that. There’s a lot that you have to do with Kevin, and you just kind of scrap that and move on to all the other stuff we worked on.” More to Read
